Only methods declared in sugar-mcp-client/src, or inherited from a parent declared there, are listed. A type that extends a class outside that tree, such as \RuntimeException, does not show the methods of that class.

SugarCraft\McpClient

ArgumentShape final class

Restores the JSON object/array distinction a tools/call argument map lost on its way into PHP, guided by the tool's own inputSchema.

MethodSummary
static conform(array $arguments, array $inputSchema): arrayThe tool-call argument map with every empty object position (per the schema) turned into \stdClass. The top level itself stays an array — an empty one is returned as [], and each transport keeps its own === [] ? new \stdClass() for the arguments member (the top-level object law), so a caller typed array (e.g. ClaudeCodeMcpClient) can take the result.

ExchangeLock final class

Cross-process mutual exclusion for one stdio connection, plus the state that must outlive whichever process held it last.

MethodSummary
static new(string $label, ?string $dir = null): selfCreate the lock file for a connection the CURRENT process owns, after sweeping the files dead owners left in the same directory.
static create(string $label, ?string $dir = null): selfFormer name of new(), kept as a public-API compatibility shim until any embedder still calling it moves over; the repo's factory rule names the default root ::new(). (The originally-named downstream caller has ALREADY migrated — the sole caller inside this repo is the alias-resolution test, and this note carries no survivor's name so it cannot go stale again.)
static sweepStale(?string $dir = null): intRemove the lock files in $dir whose owner process no longer exists.
acquire(?float $deadline, \Closure $serverAlive): boolWait for the exclusive lock. Polls LOCK_NB rather than blocking so the wait honours $deadline (hrtime seconds, null = no deadline, matching the no-deadline tool-call policy) and gives up the moment the server is gone.
load(): arrayThe phase and buffer the previous holder left.
store(string $phase, string $buffer): boolRewrite the whole state: phase byte plus buffer. This is a FULL truncate-and-write of everything the exchange carries, on every exchange, under the lock: the cost tracks the read buffer's size (bounded by the transport frame cap), a deliberate price for state an external kill can only ever leave whole-or-empty. An append-delta design would need a cross-process offset ledger to stay recoverable — it re-earns nothing the phase byte could not already say.
markPhase(string $phase): boolOverwrite the phase byte alone, leaving the stored buffer as it is.
release(): void
close(): voidClose THIS process' handle; the file and every other process' handle stay.
destroy(): voidClose, and — in the owner only — remove the file.

McpMessage final class

A single JSON-RPC 2.0 envelope — request, notification, success response or error response — as one immutable value object.

MethodSummary
static parse(string $json): ?selfParse one wire line into an envelope, or null when the payload is not a JSON-RPC 2.0 object we can act on.
static parsePreservingId(string $json): ?selfTHE ID-PRESERVING VARIANT: parse(), except that the id is also kept exactly as it arrived — an integer stays an integer — in $wireId, and toJson() writes it back that way.
withWireId(string|int|null $id): selfA copy whose wire id is $id exactly as given — how the id-preserving variant BUILDS a message: McpMessage::success((string) $id, $r)->withWireId($id) answers an integer-id request with the integer, and McpMessage::error('', $code, $m)->withWireId(null) is the "id": null error JSON-RPC requires for a request whose id could not be read. On a notification, which carries no id, it changes nothing on the wire.
static request(string $id, string $method, ?array $params = null): selfBuild an outgoing request envelope (method + id + params).
static notification(string $method, ?array $params = null): selfBuild an outgoing notification envelope (method, no id, no answer).
static success(string $id, mixed $result): selfBuild a success response. Accepts any value — MCP results are mixed and null is a legal payload, which is what resultSet records.
static error(string $id, int $code, string $message, mixed $data = null): selfBuild a JSON-RPC error envelope. An explicit wire "data": null does NOT survive a build→encode→parse round-trip: the member is omitted for a null $data, and a parsed envelope keeps only what the wire carried. Code 0 is legal and preserved — callers who mean "no data" and callers who mean "null data" both arrive at the omission; JSON-RPC treats the two alike.
toJson(): stringWire serialization — one line, no trailing newline, keys only when set.
toArray(): arrayInspection view: every key present, including the booleans and the wire-id pair.
isRequest(): boolOutgoing-shaped request: has a method, has an id, is not a notification.
isResponse(): boolA response carries no method — only result and/or error.
isNotification(): bool
isError(): bool
errorCode(): ?intThe JSON-RPC error code, or NULL when absent or malformed.
errorMessage(): ?stringThe JSON-RPC error message, or NULL when absent or malformed.

McpRouter final class

SERVER narrowing over a keyed map of MCP servers (tool rosters follow servers): deny patterns first, then an explicit allow-list.

McpServer interface

The contract every MCP server transport must honour: start, expose its tool table, answer tool calls, stop — plus the two raw RPC legs (request()/notify()) every transport speaks, so code typed against this interface can reach protocol traffic beyond the tool surface without growing a second type per transport family.

MethodSummary
start(): voidBring the server up and complete the MCP handshake (initialize → notifications/initialized → tools/list), caching the tool table.
stop(): voidTear the server down. Must be safe to call when never started and to call twice; implementations must leave no child process behind.
listTools(): arrayThe tool table captured at start(), each entry tagged with this server's name.
callTool(string $name, array $arguments): arrayInvoke a tool and return the MCP result payload as an array.
request(string $method, ?array $params = null, ?float $deadline = null): ?McpMessageOne raw request/response round trip — the leg callTool() rides, exposed for protocol traffic beyond the tool surface (resources, prompts, completion) without this contract growing speculative convenience methods.
notify(string $method, ?array $params = null, ?float $deadline = null): boolOne-way leg: send a notification, await nothing (JSON-RPC promises no reply). Same absolute-monotonic $deadline law as self::request().

McpTool final class

One tool definition advertised by an MCP server: name, description, JSON-Schema input contract, and the owning server.

MethodSummary
__construct(public readonly string $name, public readonly string $description, public readonly array $inputSchema, public readonly string $serverName, public readonly array $annotations = [])
static fromArray(array $definition, string $serverName): selfBuild from a wire tool definition. Absent or explicitly-null fields collapse to their defaults ('', []) — the ?? reads match the well-typedness gate below, which uses isset() semantics.
static tryFromArray(array $definition, string $serverName): ?selfParse-then-trust factory: null unless every wire field carries its declared type, so a malformed definition degrades to "skipped" instead of an exception at the construction subscript.

PendingCalls final class

The in-flight request table of a JSON-RPC client: register a settle callback under an id, settle it when the reply arrives, fail the whole table when the transport dies.

MethodSummary
register(string $id, \Closure $settle, bool $preserving = false): void
has(string $id): bool
isPreserving(string $id): bool
count(): int
settle(string $id, mixed $result): boolDeliver a successful result; false when $id is not pending.
fail(string $id, \Throwable $failure): boolDeliver a failure for one id; false when $id is not pending.
failAll(\Throwable|string $failure): intTransport death: fail every pending call with $failure (a string becomes a \RuntimeException) and empty the table first, so callbacks that register a retry land in a fresh table. Returns how many failed.

ProcessLiveness final class

The single home of the signal-0 liveness contract this library leans on in three places: who may claim an id sequence, whether a lock's owner still exists, and whether a forked observer still has a server to talk to. One kernel contract deserves one probe — the pre-extraction tree carried three hand-rolled variants whose fail-open shapes drifted apart, so a fix to one (say, a stricter EPERM reading) silently failed to reach the others.

MethodSummary
static ownerAlive(int $pid): boolRefuse-only-on-certainty polarity: true unless the kernel can prove the pid is absent.

RequestIdSequence final class

JSON-RPC request ids that stay unique across pcntl_fork().

MethodSummary
__construct(?\Closure $pidProvider = null, int $firstOwnerId = 0, ?\Closure $ownerAlive = null)
claim(): boolMake the CURRENT process the owner — called when a connection is opened, because the process that opened it is the one whose ids should look ordinary. The owner counter is not reset: an id is never reused within one object's lifetime, even across a stop()/start() cycle.
ownerPid(): int
isOwner(): boolIs the current process the one that opened the connection?
currentPid(): intThe current pid, as the provider reports it.
next(): int|stringThe next id: an int for the owner, a <pid>-<nonce>-<n> string for any other process. Transports that put ids on the wire as strings cast the int; a transport that historically sent integers keeps doing so for the owner. A matcher must therefore compare ids as strings.

StdioMcpServer final class

An MCP server reached over a child process' stdin/stdout, speaking newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0.

MethodSummary
__construct(public readonly string $name, private readonly string $command, private readonly array $args = [], private readonly array $env = [], ?float $startTimeoutSeconds = null, private readonly ?\Closure $spawnPlanner = null, array $clientInfo = self::DEFAULT_CLIENT_INFO, private readonly ?string $cwd = null, array $capabilities = [], ?\Closure $onServerMessage = null, private readonly ?string $lockDir = null, private readonly array $envRemove = [], private readonly ?array $curatedEnv = null, ?string $clientName = null, ?string $clientVersion = null)
__destruct()Orphan-proofing: a server the embedder forgot to stop dies with this object. stop() is idempotent, so an already-stopped instance is a no-op.
start(?\Closure $onWait = null): voidBegin the session: spawn, then run initialize → notifications/initialized → tools/list under one deadline.
stop(): voidTear the connection down: pipes first (a well-behaved server exits on stdin EOF before ever seeing a signal), then the TERM → poll → KILL → reap ladder, then the lock and the per-call state. Idempotent, and fork-aware — a non-owner clone closes only its own copies and leaves the connection to the process that started it.
stderrTail(): stringThe captured stderr tail, control characters swept. Survives stop() on purpose: a server that died is the one whose logs you want. The TEXT is server-authored and remains UNTRUSTED — render it through a sanitiser before terminal-facing display.
pumpStderr(): voidDrain pending stderr without blocking, for callers that idle between exchanges and want diagnostics warm. This is a CALLER-PUMPED seam on purpose: mounting it on an event loop would put two readers on one pipe, and pipe reads are destructive — whichever reader wins eats bytes the other was meant to see (the shared-pipe readership ruling: two readers on one pipe steal each other's bytes).
isUp(): boolIs the child process still alive?
listTools(): array
malformedToolDefinitions(): arrayLabels of the tools/list definitions refused by the well-typedness gate during the current start — the ones parseTools() skipped instead of registering. Post-mortem evidence: reset by every start(), kept by stop(). The view is capped at self::MALFORMED_LEDGER_CEILING entries; the full count rides the report.
malformedToolDefinitionsReport(): stringOne-line announcement for the skipped definitions, '' when the last tools/list walk registered everything the server advertised. Report it wherever the server's start outcome is surfaced — the roster is already SAFE (only valid definitions were registered); this is the half of the story the user must not have to guess. The count is the honest total; the named rows are the first few of a ledger capped at self::MALFORMED_LEDGER_CEILING, and a cut-off list says so with [+N more] — truncation announced, never silent.
serverInfo(): ?arrayThe server's advertised serverInfo (name, version, optional title) exactly as it answered the handshake — UNTRUSTED server-authored text: route it through Sanitize::untrusted before it reaches a terminal. Null before the first successful start(), after a start that never reached the judgement, or when the server omitted the member (see self::initializeResultDefects()). Survives stop(): "which server was this?" stays answerable post-mortem.
serverCapabilities(): ?arrayThe server's advertised capability map — the gate an embedder reads before trying resources/*, prompts/*, elicitation, or trusting a listChanged notification: null/absent means the server never claimed the feature. Same survival and untrusted-text laws as self::serverInfo().
initializeResultDefects(): arraySpec-required InitializeResult members the server failed to send (serverInfo, capabilities). The store is deliberately tolerant — a server that negotiated and listed tools boots, and these names tell the embedder WHY the accessors come back empty instead of leaving the omission unannounced. Empty list means the handshake was whole.
callTool(string $name, array $arguments, ?\Closure $onWait = null, ?float $timeoutSeconds = null, ?\Closure $onServerMessage = null): arrayInvoke a tool. No deadline by default (the no-blanket-timeout law): see the class docblock.
listResources(): arrayresources/list — the server's advertised resources. Same array-or-error shape as self::callTool(): the result payload on success, ['error' => ...] on any failure; never a throw, never null. The unbounded-wait law applies (this is protocol chatter without a defensible blanket budget — bound it via self::request() if you need a deadline).
readResource(string $uri): arrayresources/read — fetch one resource by URI.
listPrompts(): arrayprompts/list — the server's advertised prompt templates.
getPrompt(string $name, array $arguments = []): arrayprompts/get — render one prompt template. $arguments follows the tool-arguments law: an object map, a non-empty positional list is refused at the client door, and [] is repaired to an empty JSON object before the wire sees it.
request(string $method, ?array $params = null, ?float $deadline = null, ?\Closure $onServerMessage = null): ?McpMessageOne request/response round trip. Public so protocol traffic beyond tools (resources/list, prompts/get, completion) is one call away for embedders without this library growing that surface speculatively — the product implements none of it either.
notify(string $method, ?array $params = null, ?float $deadline = null): boolNotification leg of the protocol: no reply is awaited, but delivery is reported — true once the whole line went out, false when it did not (not started, dead pipe, lock or $deadline lost), so an embedder sending notifications/cancelled or progress can tell a dropped one.
writeFramed(string $json, ?float $deadline = null): boolPublic framing primitive: write exactly one newline-delimited JSON-RPC frame (payload + "\n") under an optional monotonic deadline, absorbing stderr while waiting for write-readiness — the same drain law every internal leg obeys, so a full stderr pipe can never wedge this side.
static monotonicNow(): floatThe clock every $deadline in this class is measured on: monotonic seconds since an arbitrary boot-relative origin (hrtime), never wall clock, never rewound by an NTP step (a handshake bound must ride a clock that only moves forward, matching sugar-core BoundedShutdown's own hrtime basis). Public so elapsed-time arithmetic is possible; to BOUND a wait, prefer self::deadlineAfter() over hand-adding.
static deadlineAfter(float $seconds): floatThe seatbelt for the two deadline idioms: self::request() and self::notify() take an ABSOLUTE monotonic instant while self::callTool() takes a RELATIVE duration — mixing them up (passing a duration where an instant belongs) fails quietly, because a small boot-relative instant sits in the past and the wait simply never starts, or a wall-clock magnitude can never be reached. This helper turns "how long" into "until when" on the one basis this class reads, so embedders never hand-combine the idioms.

A candy-code.v1 method's refusal: thrown by a method, answered by the Dispatcher as a JSON-RPC error object whose data.kind is the machine-readable reason (Appendix O §6.2). Nothing a client sent is echoed in the message; data carries only what the method chose to put there.
